fields.title: [Ueno] Gong cha Opens at Marui Ueno on August 8!
fields.summary: Taiwanese tea drink specialist Gong cha opens a new store on the 1st floor of Marui Ueno.
fields.body:
Gong cha, a tea drink specialist from Taiwan, will open on the 1st floor of Marui Ueno on August 8, 2026. The popular chain operates in countries around the world and has been steadily opening stores in Japan, mainly in central Tokyo. This will be its first store in the Ueno area.

The menu offers a wide lineup, from the signature Milk Foam Tea to milk teas, fruit teas and seasonal flavors, along with plenty of toppings such as tapioca pearls and nata de coco. Menu items exclusive to the Ueno store are also planned, and the shop is expected to become a popular new place to take a break for local workers and tourists alike.

Marui Ueno sits in a prime location right in front of Ueno Station, which makes it easy to drop by while shopping or dining. Lines are expected right after the opening, so plan to allow extra time when you visit.

Store Information
- Name: Gong cha Marui Ueno
- Address: Marui Ueno 1F, 6-15-1 Ueno, Taito-ku, Tokyo
- Hours: 11:00-21:00
- Opening date: August 8, 2026
- Access: Right next to JR Ueno Station

fields.title: [Ueno] Ueno Spice Curry Shokudo Opens August 20!
fields.summary: A new restaurant serving authentic spice curry arrives in the Ueno-Hirokoji area.
fields.body:
Ueno Spice Curry Shokudo, a restaurant specializing in authentic spice curry, will open in the Ueno-Hirokoji area on August 20, 2026. The new restaurant focuses on spice curry, which has grown in popularity in recent years. It will prepare several spice curries, including chicken, keema and vegetable, on a daily rotating basis and serve fragrant, aromatic dishes.

At lunchtime, it will serve filling set meals. In the evening, it plans to offer an ai-mori platter with small portions of several curries. It is set to become a new option in Ueno-Hirokoji, an area packed with restaurants. Takeout is expected to be available, and the restaurant expects to draw office workers from nearby.

Store Information
- Name: Ueno Spice Curry Shokudo
- Address: 2-3-4 Ueno, Taito-ku, Tokyo

fields.title: [Ueno] Summer Night Market Coming to Ueno Park from August 21!
fields.summary: A night market will be held at Ueno Park over three days.
fields.body:
The "Summer Night Market" will be held at the Fountain Plaza in Ueno Park from August 21 to 23, 2026. Local restaurants and craft artists will set up stalls, bringing lively crowds to the park from evening into the night.

The venue will feature booths selling handmade accessories and goods, along with food from food trucks. Once it cools down in the evening, visitors can enjoy the market while strolling through the illuminated park. Since it falls on a weekend near the end of summer vacation, a wide range of visitors, including families and couples, is expected.

In case of rain, parts of the program may change, so checking the official website for the latest information is recommended. The event also pairs well with a visit to the museums and art galleries around Ueno Park.

- Venue: Fountain Plaza, Ueno Park

fields.title: [Ueno] "The Lineage of Modern Japanese Art" Opens at the Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum
fields.summary: A special exhibition tracing Japanese art from the Meiji era to the early Showa era has opened.
fields.body:
The special exhibition "The Lineage of Modern Japanese Art" opened at the Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum on August 15, 2026. It runs until October 12.

The exhibition traces how Japanese art changed from the Meiji era to the early Showa era. Through works in a wide range of genres, including Western-style painting, Nihonga (Japanese-style painting) and sculpture, it shows how the adoption of Western art and the continuation of traditional techniques shaped each other. Many rare works have been gathered from museums in Japan and abroad and from private collections, and some pieces can only be seen at this exhibition.

Gallery talks by curators and audio guide rentals are planned during the exhibition, so it is a good choice for visitors who want to take their time. Ueno Park is also home to several other art museums and museums, so visiting a few of them in one trip is another way to enjoy the area.

Event Information
- Dates: August 15 – October 12, 2026
- Venue: Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum
- Admission: General 2,000 yen
- Access: 7-minute walk from the Park Exit of JR Ueno Station

fields.title: [Ueno] "Dinosaur Expo 2026" Now On at the National Museum of Nature and Science
fields.summary: A special exhibition of dinosaur fossils and life-size reconstructions based on the latest research.
fields.body:
"Dinosaur Expo 2026" is now on at the National Museum of Nature and Science. It shows dinosaur fossils and reconstruction models based on the latest research. The exhibition runs until September 27.

Highlights include full skeletons of large carnivorous dinosaurs. Panels explain what recent excavations have revealed about how dinosaurs lived and evolved, and finely made reconstruction models are also on display. A hands-on area for children lets visitors touch fossil replicas and watch videos that recreate dinosaur calls and movements, so families can enjoy the exhibition together.

The exhibition overlaps with the summer holidays, so crowds are expected, especially on weekends. Timed-entry tickets and advance online booking are recommended. To avoid the crowds, visit on a weekday morning.

Event Information
- Dates: July 19 – September 27, 2026
- Venue: National Museum of Nature and Science
- Admission: Adults 2,100 yen
- Access: 5-minute walk from the Park Exit of JR Ueno Station

The lineup focuses on waterproof makeup that stands up to sweat and oil, along with UV care products, and ranges from buzzworthy up-and-coming brands to popular classics. fields.body:
Compact Select ecute Ueno, a general goods store in ecute Ueno, has announced that it will close on September 30, 2026. A closing sale is also planned.

Located inside Ueno Station, the store has been a convenient stop for travelers and commuters. Ahead of the closure, discount sales on items in stock are expected to take place in stages, and more regulars will likely stop by in search of bargains.

No details have been announced yet about what will replace the store, and many are watching for news of a new tenant. For longtime fans, the closure is sad news.

fields.title: [Ueno] Panda Keeper Talk Event at Ueno Zoo
fields.summary: On August 22, zookeepers will give a special talk in front of the Panda House.
fields.body:
Ueno Zoo will hold a talk event by its zookeepers in front of the Panda House on August 22, 2026. The talk will introduce the pandas' behavior and ecology and take a behind-the-scenes look at their care.

The keepers who look after the pandas plan to explain what the animals usually eat, how they spend their day, and how their health is managed, with quizzes along the way to keep it easy to follow. A Q&A session for visitors is also expected. It is a rare chance to hear firsthand information that only the zoo can offer.

Because the event falls during the summer holidays, many families are expected to visit, and the area around the Panda House will likely be crowded during the event. If you want a good viewing spot, arrive well before the start time.

Event Information
- Date: August 22, 2026
- Venue: In front of the Panda House, Ueno Zoo
- Fee: Zoo admission only
- Access: 5-minute walk from the Park Exit of JR Ueno Station

fields.title: [Ueno] Ueno Book Cafe Leaf Celebrates First Anniversary with Community Event
fields.summary: A local bookstore cafe held a talk event to mark its first anniversary.
fields.body:
Ueno Book Cafe Leaf, located in front of Ueno Station, marked its first anniversary in July 2026 with a talk event featuring a local author. Combining a bookstore and a cafe, the shop has gradually built a following among local residents and book lovers as a place to relax with a book in hand.

The event welcomed an author who lives in the area as a guest, who shared stories about their creative work and their feelings for the Ueno neighborhood. It was a relaxed gathering that encouraged interaction with attendees. The shop also sold a limited-edition anniversary coffee blend and original merchandise, drawing a lively crowd made up mostly of regulars.

The shop plans to continue holding events regularly, and further growth is expected as a bookstore cafe rooted in the community.

# "Kyukyasu": Reliable Spot Work That "Connects" People Inside the Station

## Overview

"Kyukyasu" is a new spot work service in the Ueno area that operates from inside train stations. As the word "reliable" in its name suggests, it offers spot work, which has grown popular in recent years. With spot work, people take jobs when and for as long as they choose, without being tied to a fixed workplace or schedule. The service runs from a very convenient location: inside the station itself.

Spot work refers to one-off or short-hours jobs. It has drawn attention both from people who want to make good use of their free time and from businesses that need temporary staff, for example during busy periods. Kyukyasu builds on this trend. It connects workers with jobs inside stations, where many people pass through every day to commute, go to school or shop.

As the word "connects" suggests, the service does more than list jobs. Its key feature is that it matches people who want to work with workplaces that need staff, and it does this within the station, a natural part of people's daily routes. Because it is based inside the station, the service is also easy to use between commutes or classes, or while out running errands.

Ueno is a major transport hub where Shinkansen, JR and subway lines meet, and its busy terminal station sees heavy foot traffic every day. Given these crowds, a spot work service based inside the station is an initiative that reflects Ueno's local character.

fields.body:
[Ueno] Lecture "Picture Books Using Monochrome Expression" on November 15, hosted by the International Library of Children's Literature

Overview

The International Library of Children's Literature will hold a lecture titled "Picture Books Using Monochrome Expression" on November 15, 2026.

The lecture focuses on monochrome, a picture book technique that uses no color, only black and white (or shades of a single color). Without color, monochrome illustration relies on line, shading and the use of white space to convey a story's atmosphere and its characters' emotions. It is considered an important area of picture book making. The lecture will take an expert look at picture books that use monochrome expression.

The event is mainly for junior high school students and older. Rather than being aimed at children, it is designed for a wide audience, from middle and high school students to adults, with an interest in picture book art, fine art, publishing or education. Many people think of picture books as something for children, but a lecture that explores the techniques behind them offers plenty to learn for anyone involved in creating books or wanting to study picture books.

Capacity is 100, with advance registration on a first-come, first-served basis. At the time of writing, registration has not opened, so anyone wishing to attend will need to wait for the announcement. Because registration closes once the limit is reached, those interested should keep an eye out for updates.

The International Library of Children's Literature is known for regularly organizing events about children's books and picture books, and this lecture is part of that work. By focusing on monochrome, a deliberately limited palette, instead of color, the lecture promises to broaden the ways we read and look at picture books.

fields.title: FY2026 Special Training Course "Promoting Barrier-Free Reading" (On-Demand Streaming)
fields.summary: For librarians, school staff, families of children with disabilities and others. Capacity 1,000 (first come, first served). Registration is closed.
fields.body:
[Ueno] FY2026 Special Training Course "Promoting Barrier-Free Reading" Streams On Demand from August 6

Overview

The FY2026 special training course "Promoting Barrier-Free Reading" is being held in the Ueno area. It is aimed at librarians, school staff, families of children with disabilities and others, and covers a timely topic: making reading environments barrier-free.

Barrier-free reading means creating an environment where everyone can enjoy reading equally, whether or not they have a visual, hearing, physical, developmental or other disability. Libraries and schools are increasingly expected to provide a range of formats, such as Braille materials, audio materials, large-print books and DAISY books, and to give thoughtful support to users and students with disabilities. For librarians and school staff who deal with these issues every day, a chance to gain specialist knowledge is valuable. For families raising children with disabilities, learning practical ways to help their children enjoy reading is a matter of everyday concern. The course is designed so that participants from these different backgrounds can learn about the same topic together.

Another feature is the format: the course is streamed on demand instead of being held at a venue. Participants can watch at any convenient time within the set viewing period, from work, home or anywhere else. Librarians and school staff often have to fit learning in around their daily work, and families of children with disabilities may find it hard to attend a venue at a fixed date and time. The on-demand format appears designed to accommodate these needs.

The course had a capacity of 1,000 participants, with registration on a first-come, first-served basis. Registration has now closed, and new applications are no longer accepted. Interested readers may want to watch for related updates and for similar courses in future years.

[Ueno] Special Display "Collection in Focus" Opens March 28 at the National Museum of Western Art

Overview

The National Museum of Western Art will hold "Collection in Focus," a special display within its permanent collection galleries. It will be on the 2nd floor of the Main Building and the 1st floor of the New Wing, and presents a narrowed selection of works from the permanent collection.

Located in Ueno Park, the National Museum of Western Art is one of Japan's leading museums dedicated to Western art. Its collection covers a wide range of periods and media, including paintings, sculptures and prints from the late Middle Ages to the early 20th century. The museum draws on the depth of this collection to rotate its permanent exhibition, changing the themes and approaches over time. "Collection in Focus" is one of these special displays.

As the title suggests, the display looks again at works from the permanent collection from a specific perspective and brings together their highlights. The display is spread across two floors, the 2nd floor of the Main Building and the 1st floor of the New Wing, so visitors can see it as they move through the permanent collection galleries, a layout typical of the museum.

The display is scheduled to run from March 28, 2026 to mid-January 2027, a long run of about 10 months. The Ueno Park area is also home to many other cultural and tourist attractions, including the Tokyo National Museum, the Tokyo Metropolitan Art Museum and Ueno Zoo, so you can also explore the neighborhood when you visit the National Museum of Western Art.

fields.title: [Special Exhibit] "Showa 100": The History of Conservation and Restoration at the Museum in the Showa Era — Van Gogh's Roses and Renoir's Woman with a Hat as Examples
fields.summary: Marking the 100th year since the start of the Showa era, this special exhibit traces how conservation and restoration practices changed at the museum, using two works from its collection as examples: Van Gogh's Roses and Renoir's Woman with a Hat. It is held in the 19th-Century Hall on the 1st floor of the Main Building.
fields.body:
[Ueno] Special exhibit "Showa 100": The History of Conservation and Restoration at the Museum in the Showa Era opens June 30 in the 19th-Century Hall, Main Building 1F

Overview

From June 30, 2026 to January 11, 2027, the special exhibit "Showa 100": The History of Conservation and Restoration at the Museum in the Showa Era — Van Gogh's Roses and Renoir's Woman with a Hat as Examples will be held in the 19th-Century Hall on the 1st floor of the Main Building in Ueno.

The exhibit marks the milestone of the 100th year since the Showa era began. It centers on two works from the museum's collection, Vincent van Gogh's Roses and Pierre-Auguste Renoir's Woman with a Hat, and traces the conservation and restoration work the museum carried out over the course of the Showa era.

Over time, Western paintings change as their paint deteriorates and their surfaces become damaged. Conservation and restoration work is essential to identify these changes, give the works the treatment they need and pass them on to future generations. As concrete examples, the exhibit features two of the museum's signature works, Van Gogh's Roses and Renoir's Woman with a Hat. Both were painted by artists central to any discussion of modern Western painting, and both have long been popular with visitors. The exhibit shows the conservation and restoration processes these works went through during the Showa era, giving visitors a way to engage with the paintings from a different angle than simply viewing them.

The venue, the 19th-Century Hall on the 1st floor of the Main Building, is a permanent gallery devoted mainly to 19th-century Western painting, and the special exhibit is presented within this space. A highlight of the exhibit is the chance to view works by Van Gogh and Renoir in person while learning the history of the specialized conservation and restoration work behind them.

The exhibit runs for more than six months, from June 30, 2026 to January 11, 2027. If you're planning to see art in Ueno, consider adding it to your visit.

[Ueno] Myth, Allegory, and Festivity: Italian Courts and Prints from the Renaissance to the Baroque — From June 30 in the Prints and Drawings Gallery

Overview

The small-scale exhibition "Myth, Allegory, and Festivity: Italian Courts and Prints from the Renaissance to the Baroque" focuses on the prints that adorned Italian courts from the Renaissance through the Baroque. The venue is the Prints and Drawings Gallery (Permanent Collection Galleries, New Wing 2F).

Courts across Italy produced large numbers of prints depicting mythological and allegorical subjects, as well as prints recording festivities. Whether as a means of displaying the prestige of those in power or of passing the memory of celebrations on to later generations, prints were closely tied to the court culture of the time. Through these works, the exhibition sheds light on the visual culture fostered by Italian courts during the transition from the Renaissance to the Baroque. Because it is held in the Prints and Drawings Gallery, a section within the Permanent Collection Galleries, visitors can view it together with the other permanent exhibits.

A shop specializing in Taiwanese castella has opened in the Ueno area. Taiwanese castella is a sponge cake made with lots of eggs and baked slowly at a low temperature. The new Ueno shop stands out for recreating the traditional Taiwanese recipe exactly, and it has drawn attention for offering the same taste and texture you would find in Taiwan.

fields.title: [Special Exhibition] Glass Dry Plate Exhibition: The Joy of Taking Photographs
fields.summary: The invention of the glass dry plate opened photography to the general public. Drawing on glass plates in the museum's collection, the exhibition presents street scenes, travel snapshots and family photos taken by amateur photographers. Its theme is the first step toward the popularization of photography.
fields.body:
[Ueno] Special Exhibition "Glass Dry Plate Exhibition: The Joy of Taking Photographs" Opens March 3 at the Shitamachi Museum

Overview

The special exhibition "Glass Dry Plate Exhibition: The Joy of Taking Photographs" opens at the Shitamachi Museum in Ueno on March 3, 2026.

The exhibition looks at how the invention of the glass dry plate opened photography up to the general public. Photography once required specialized skills and equipment, and the glass dry plate is known as the technology that put it within reach of many more people. Visitors can explore its historical significance through actual materials.

On display is a selection of photographs taken by amateur photographers of the era, drawn from the glass plates in the Shitamachi Museum's collection. Subjects vary widely, from snapshots of street scenes to records of trips and everyday family moments. Unlike work by professional photographers, these images convey the atmosphere of a time when photography was starting to take root in people's lives as a hobby.

The exhibition's theme is "the first step toward the popularization of photography." Through the museum's collection, it traces how the glass dry plate, a technological innovation, turned photography from something special into something familiar to ordinary people. What did ordinary people look at, and what did they try to record, once they had a camera in hand? The exhibition promises a rare chance to see the world through the eyes of the amateur photographers of the time.

[Ueno] Mural "Asakusa Big Parade" Exhibition at the Shitamachi Museum from July 7!

Overview

This special exhibition shows the mural "Asakusa Big Parade" by Koji Kata. The mural once decorated the inside of a coffee shop in Nishi-Asakusa 3-chome. The exhibition also presents materials on the Asakusa stars painted in the mural. Together with the mural, these materials look back at the entertainers and celebrities who brought color to Asakusa in its heyday.

The exhibition also features "Golden Bat," Kata's best-known work, and uses it to explain the culture of street kamishibai (picture-card storytelling). In the Showa era, kamishibai was a popular form of entertainment for children on street corners, and "Golden Bat" is known as one of its most famous works. The exhibition traces the mural artist's career alongside the culture of kamishibai.

fields.summary: An exhibition centered on rarely shown paper materials from the museum's collection, such as nishiki-e woodblock prints and picture postcards, introducing the visual culture once enjoyed by ordinary people.
fields.body:
[Ueno] Special Exhibition "Collection Exhibition (Tentative Title)" Opens November 3 at the Shitamachi Museum

The special exhibition "Collection Exhibition (Tentative Title)" will be held at the Shitamachi Museum in Ueno from November 3, 2026 to February 28, 2027.

Overview

This exhibition focuses on paper materials from the Shitamachi Museum's collection that have rarely been shown to the public, such as nishiki-e and picture postcards. Nishiki-e are multicolored woodblock prints that circulated widely among ordinary people from the Edo period through the Meiji era, popular as a vivid medium for conveying the news, trends, customs and famous sights of the day. Picture postcards, too, spread alongside advances in photography and printing, becoming part of everyday life as an easy way to share scenes from travels and views of the city.

Although such paper materials are valuable records that convey the atmosphere of their times and how people lived, the fragile nature of paper means that, out of concern for their preservation, they are seldom placed on permanent display, and opportunities to see them have been limited. Through these items from the collection, the exhibition introduces the visual culture once enjoyed by ordinary people. It promises to be a chance to see materials that are rarely on view.

The Shitamachi Museum is known as a facility that conveys the history and culture of the Ueno and shitamachi (old downtown) area, and it holds a large collection of items related to local life. This special exhibition offers a rare opportunity to explore part of that collection.

fields.body:
[Ueno] Taito City 80th Anniversary Project: The History of Taito City Exhibition (Tentative Title) Opens March 2, 2027 at the Shitamachi Museum

Overview

"The History of Taito City Exhibition (Tentative Title)" will be held at the Shitamachi Museum to mark the 80th anniversary of Taito City, which includes the Ueno and Asakusa areas.

Taito City was created by the merger of Shitaya Ward and Asakusa Ward, which were once separate municipalities. The exhibition first introduces these two wards as they were before the merger, focusing on the history of each and the distinctive character of each area. It will look back at the local character and features of both wards, which developed against the backdrop of shitamachi (old downtown) culture dating back to the Edo period.

The exhibition then traces the 80 years since the two wards merged to form Taito City. It introduces events from the city's history, how its streets and neighborhoods changed over time, and what Taito City looks like today, giving visitors an overview of how the area has changed over many years.

Taito City, home to Ueno and Asakusa, is known for areas that still keep the atmosphere of old downtown Tokyo, and this look back at its origins and history should be well worth a visit for anyone interested in local history. A key feature of the exhibition is that a single show traces the story from the days of Shitaya Ward and Asakusa Ward to the present, offering a fresh chance to learn how Taito City came to be.

The venue, the Shitamachi Museum, presents the history and culture of Tokyo's shitamachi area and has previously held special exhibitions on local themes. This exhibition is part of a commemorative project marking Taito City's 80th anniversary.

fields.title: 10th Anniversary of World Heritage Inscription Lecture: "The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier, an Outstanding Contribution to the Modern Movement"
fields.summary: A lecture marking the 10th anniversary of the National Museum of Western Art's inscription as a World Heritage Site. Advance registration required; applications are expected to open in early October.
fields.body:
[Ueno] Lecture "The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier" Marks 10 Years Since World Heritage Inscription! From November 29 at Taito City Lifelong Learning Center

The National Museum of Western Art in Ueno Park is known for its Main Building, designed by the French architect Le Corbusier. In 2016, it was inscribed as one of the component sites of the World Cultural Heritage property "The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier, an Outstanding Contribution to the Modern Movement." The inscription drew attention for listing 17 works across seven countries together, and the National Museum of Western Art is the only component site in Japan.

2026 marks the 10th anniversary of this inscription. To celebrate, a lecture titled "10th Anniversary of World Heritage Inscription Lecture: 'The Architectural Work of Le Corbusier, an Outstanding Contribution to the Modern Movement'" will be held in Ueno. Le Corbusier was one of the leading architects of the 20th century, and his works, which used reinforced concrete and modern building techniques, are said to have greatly influenced later architectural movements around the world. The National Museum of Western Art is his only building in Japan, so the lecture is also a good opportunity to reflect on the presence of a world-class architectural heritage site in Ueno.

The venue is Millennium Hall at Taito City Lifelong Learning Center in the Ueno area. The center serves as a local hub for lifelong learning and hosts a variety of courses and events.

Advance registration is required, and applications are scheduled to open in early October 2026. Further details, such as how to apply and the exact opening date and time, have yet to be announced.

The lecture is a must for anyone interested in architecture or art, as well as for those who want to learn more about the value of the World Heritage Site in Ueno. Why not attend this special event held for the 10th anniversary?

# Former Tokyo Music School Sogakudo Announces September Building Open Days

The Former Tokyo Music School Sogakudo, located in a corner of Ueno Park next to Tokyo University of the Arts, has announced its building open days for September 2026. Built in the Meiji era, the Sogakudo is a wooden concert hall known as a building that tells the history of modern music education in Japan. It is a valuable piece of architecture that preserves its original design and structure, and one of the spots worth visiting when you come to Ueno.

Open days are scheduled throughout the month, giving visitors a chance to see the building's interior and fittings that retain the atmosphere of the era. Note, however, that because the building dates from the Meiji era, it is not barrier-free. Its structure, including steps and the presence or absence of ramps, differs from modern facilities, so it's a good idea to check in advance against your own means of getting around and physical condition before visiting.

Photography inside the hall is also not permitted while on-stage rehearsals or concerts are taking place. The Sogakudo is still in active use as a concert hall, so even on open days you cannot always photograph freely throughout the entire hall. This is a circumstance unique to a historic building that balances musical performances with public access.

Standing in a Meiji-era wooden hall where musicians of the time studied and performed is an experience only Ueno can offer. Check the open-day schedule and be sure to pay a visit.

Shimantoya Ueno, a new restaurant serving straw-grilled dishes, donabe clay-pot rice and sake, opened in the Ueno area on September 1, 2026. As the name suggests, the restaurant appears to have ties to the Shimanto River, a clear-water river in Kochi Prefecture, and its signature is warayaki, a dramatic straw-grilling technique. In warayaki, straw is set ablaze and the ingredients are seared quickly over the fierce flames, giving the surface a fragrant, smoky aroma while keeping the inside moist. The technique is often used for dishes such as katsuo no tataki (seared bonito) and is popular for its distinctive smoky flavor, which differs from charcoal grilling.

The restaurant also serves donabe rice. Cooked carefully one portion at a time in a clay pot, it is prized for its freshly cooked aroma and firm, distinct grains, and should pair well with the straw-grilled dishes. Sake is also on offer, suggesting a restaurant designed for slowly savoring the smoky flavor of the grilled dishes and the richness of the clay-pot rice alongside sake. With grilled dishes, rice and drinks all covered, it caters both to diners looking for a meal and to those who want to enjoy a drink, and is expected to draw locals and tourists alike.

fields.title: Special Exhibition Commemorating the Donation of the Susumu Uchiyama Collection: "Utagawa Hiroshige: The Best Angles of Edo"
fields.summary: A special exhibition at the Tokyo National Museum commemorating the donation of the Susumu Uchiyama Collection.
fields.body:
[Ueno] Special Exhibition "Utagawa Hiroshige: The Best Angles of Edo" Opens September 29 at the Tokyo National Museum

Overview

The Tokyo National Museum is holding the special exhibition "Commemorating the Donation of the Susumu Uchiyama Collection: Utagawa Hiroshige, The Best Angles of Edo." The exhibition marks the donation of the Susumu Uchiyama Collection and presents works by Utagawa Hiroshige, one of the leading ukiyo-e artists of the Edo period.

Hiroshige is known for depicting the landscapes and famous sights of Edo from his own distinctive perspective. As the phrase "The Best Angles of Edo" in the title suggests, the exhibition appears to focus on the highlights of the Edo scenery that Hiroshige captured. It was organized to commemorate the donation of the Susumu Uchiyama Collection to the Tokyo National Museum, and works selected from the collection are expected to be on display.

The venue, the Tokyo National Museum, is located in Ueno Park and is one of Japan's leading museums. It holds and exhibits cultural properties across a wide range of fields, including Japanese and Asian art and archaeological artifacts, and draws large crowds for each special exhibition. The Ueno area is known for its concentration of cultural facilities such as museums, art galleries and a zoo, so this special exhibition is also a good opportunity to visit other cultural facilities nearby.

The exhibition runs for about three months, from September 29 to December 20, 2026. Because it continues from autumn into winter, it is easy to fit into your plans when visiting Ueno Park, including during the autumn foliage season. Through Hiroshige's works, it promises to be a valuable opportunity to see the landscapes that people of the Edo period saw and to experience the charm of Edo at that time.

Event Information
- Dates: September 29, 2026 – December 20, 2026
- Venue: Tokyo National Museum
- Official URL: https://www.kensetsu.metro.tokyo.lg.jp/jimusho/toubuk/ueno/event

Akafuku Sells Summer-Only "Akafuku Mizu Yokan" at Matsuzakaya Ueno for the First Time

Akafuku, a long-established Japanese confectioner from Ise in Mie Prefecture, will sell its summer-only "Akafuku Mizu Yokan" at Matsuzakaya Ueno for the first time. Founded in the Edo period, Akafuku is known across Japan for its signature "Akafuku Mochi," rice cake topped with smooth red bean paste. The sweet has long been a popular souvenir for visitors to Ise Grand Shrine, and the company also puts effort into seasonal limited-edition products. "Akafuku Mizu Yokan," now arriving in Ueno, is one of its summer-only items, and this is the first time it has been sold at Matsuzakaya Ueno.

From September 10, it will also be sold at the store's "Autumn Gourmet Fair." The fair brings together specialty foods and famous sweets from across Japan and is popular with shoppers and food lovers visiting Ueno. With Akafuku offering a seasonal mizu yokan as well as its classic Akafuku Mochi, visitors will have a new option to choose from.

It is a chance to easily enjoy the taste of a long-established confectioner in Ueno, and it is likely to draw attention from fans of Japanese sweets and people shopping for souvenirs.

fields.summary: Kan'eiji, the head temple in Ueno, Tokyo, known for its ties to the Tokugawa shogun family, has begun offering an autumn-limited "Tokugawa Kirie Goshuin."
fields.body:
# Kan'eiji Temple Begins Offering Autumn-Limited "Tokugawa Kirie Goshuin"

## Overview

Kan'eiji, the head temple (Daihonzan) in Ueno, Tokyo, has begun offering an autumn-limited "Tokugawa Kirie Goshuin." Kan'eiji is known for its ties to the Tokugawa shogun family and is a historic temple that has been closely connected with the Tokugawa clan since the Edo period. The new "Tokugawa Kirie Goshuin" is an autumn-limited goshuin (temple seal) that reflects this connection to the Tokugawa shoguns.

Located in Ueno, Kan'eiji carries on its link to the Tokugawa shogun family today and has drawn attention from many worshippers and people interested in history and temple and shrine culture. This new "Tokugawa Kirie Goshuin" reflects the temple's heritage. Unlike standard goshuin written in ink, kirie goshuin feature delicate paper-cut designs, often themed around the seasons or a temple's history. This one is described as "autumn-limited," suggesting it is offered to match the season.

Besides Kan'eiji, the Ueno area is dotted with temples, shrines and cultural facilities, and many visitors stop by as part of a temple visit or a stroll. A seasonal goshuin for autumn at Kan'eiji, a site with deep historical ties to the Tokugawa shoguns, is likely to draw interest as a chance to learn about the temple's history and heritage.

Details such as the offering period, fee (hatsuhoryo), address and official website have not yet been announced; further updates are awaited.

## Basic Information

- Facility: Kan'eiji Temple (Daihonzan)
- Area: Ueno
- Details: Now offering the autumn-limited "Tokugawa Kirie Goshuin"

Bridal jewelry brand TOWA has opened "TOWA Tokyo," its first directly operated store, in Okachimachi. Until now, TOWA had no stores of its own and sold mainly through department stores and select shops. The Okachimachi location is the brand's first standalone street-front store and its first directly operated shop.

Okachimachi has long been known as a "jewelry town," home to many wholesalers of jewelry and precious metals and to jewelry workshops. Many shoppers come to the area for bridal jewelry such as engagement and wedding rings. Given this, TOWA's choice of Okachimachi for its first directly operated store carries symbolic meaning for a brand that specializes in bridal jewelry.

Until now, TOWA products were only available through other retailers. The new store lets customers take their time choosing pieces in a space that more fully reflects the brand's world. Wedding and engagement rings mark a milestone in life, so a store where customers can consult at length with knowledgeable staff is likely to be a reassuring option for anyone considering a purchase.

The store is worth watching as a new stop for people touring jewelry shops in the Ueno and Okachimachi area, and as a place for engaged couples to choose their rings.

A limited-time attraction, the "Gekirei Coaster," is being held at the Ueno Zokuzoku Summer Festival. It is part of the festival organized by Joypolis and Sports X, and was created as a hands-on way to cool off during this period of lingering, intense late-summer heat.

With the heat showing no sign of easing even as summer draws to a close, hands-on attractions like this look set to be a great chance for anyone seeking a moment of refreshment, whether indoors or outdoors.

The Ueno Zokuzoku Summer Festival itself combines attractions from two different fields, Joypolis and Sports X, and the "Gekirei Coaster" is one of its limited-time offerings. Adding a cooling-themed hands-on attraction to a summer festival format appears aimed at combining heat relief with a seasonal event.

# Spring TOKYO Instagram Photo Contest 2026

The "Spring TOKYO Instagram Photo Contest 2026" will be held across Tokyo's metropolitan parks, including Kyu-Iwasaki-tei Garden in the Ueno area. Visitors use a camera or smartphone to capture the scenery and seasonal character of parks across the city, then share their photos on Instagram. Along the way, participants can rediscover each park's appeal from their own point of view.

In the Ueno area, Kyu-Iwasaki-tei Garden is one of the participating sites. With the garden joining this park-wide initiative, people visiting Ueno get one more way to enjoy the area. Kokakaitori Otakaraya, a shop specializing in buying precious metals, luxury brand goods and more, is opening a new store inside Ueno Marui, a shopping complex in Ueno, Taito-ku, Tokyo. It is operated by e-Frann Co., Ltd., which runs buyback businesses across Japan. Otakaraya is the company's chain of specialist buyback stores, and as its name suggests ("kokakaitori" means "high-price buying"), the brand promises high purchase prices.

Ueno Marui is one of the Ueno area's leading shopping complexes, conveniently accessible from JR Ueno Station, Keisei Ueno Station, and Ueno, Ueno-hirokoji and Naka-okachimachi stations on various subway lines. It houses a wide range of tenants, including fashion and lifestyle goods, and draws many people for everything from everyday shopping to special occasions. With a buyback store opening in such a busy complex, visitors to Ueno will gain a new place where they can easily drop off unwanted items, precious metals, brand goods and more while they are out.

Demand for buyback stores has grown in recent years as an option for letting go of belongings, alongside flea market apps and secondhand shops, and opening inside shopping complexes makes them more convenient for customers. By setting up shop in Ueno Marui, a facility that attracts large crowds, the store is expected to draw not only people already considering selling items but also shoppers who stop by while visiting the complex.

The opening of e-Frann's Kokakaitori Otakaraya in the Ueno area adds a new option to Ueno Marui's store lineup. Further details, such as business hours and the opening date, are expected to be announced as store information becomes available.

## Kasho Fugetsu of Ibaraki Brings "Phantom Chestnut" Yokan to Matsuzakaya Ueno, Timed to Japanese Chestnut Day on September 30

### Overview

Kasho Fugetsu, a Japanese confectionery shop from Ibaraki, will sell yokan made with a "phantom chestnut" at Matsuzakaya Ueno. The sale is timed to Japanese Chestnut Day (Wagurinohi) on September 30.

The chestnut has a Geographical Indication (GI) registration from the Japanese government and is said to grow "only one nut per burr." Under the GI protection system, the government protects the names of agricultural, forestry and fishery products and foods whose quality and characteristics come from the region where they are produced. A GI registration is official recognition that a product has qualities unique to its region.

A chestnut burr usually holds several nuts, so a single nut per burr sets this chestnut apart. That is likely why it is called the "phantom chestnut." Kasho Fugetsu has turned these precious chestnuts into yokan.

### An Autumn Japanese Sweet for Japanese Chestnut Day

September 30 is Japanese Chestnut Day, and this sale was planned to match it. Chestnuts are one of autumn's signature flavors, and in Japanese confectionery they are a favorite ingredient for evoking the season. Japanese Chestnut Day gives shoppers in Ueno a chance to pick up yokan made with GI-registered chestnuts.

Yokan keeps well and is easy to slice and share. It makes a good treat at home and could also catch the eye of anyone looking for an autumn gift.

The yokan will be sold at Matsuzakaya Ueno, a department store in Ueno. Kasho Fugetsu is normally based in Ibaraki, so this is a chance to buy its sweets in Ueno. fields.summary: To mark Japanese Chestnut Day (September 30), chestnut yokan from Kasho Fugetsu, a confectioner in Ibaraki, is coming to Matsuzakaya Ueno. The yokan is made with a GI-registered chestnut known for having "only one nut per burr."
fields.body:
## Chestnut Yokan from Ibaraki Arrives in Ueno for Japanese Chestnut Day

To mark Japanese Chestnut Day on September 30, the "Chestnut Yokan" from Kasho Fugetsu, a confectioner in Ibaraki Prefecture, is coming to Matsuzakaya Ueno. The yokan is made with a chestnut listed under Japan's GI (Geographical Indication) system and known for having "only one nut per burr." Rare enough to be called a "phantom chestnut," it is the star of this sweet, now on the shelves of Ueno's long-established department store.

### What Is Japanese Chestnut Day?

September 30 is Japanese Chestnut Day. Late September is when Japanese chestnuts come into season. This traditional sweet is being introduced for the day, a chance to enjoy one of autumn's classic flavors.

### A GI-Registered Chestnut with "Only One Nut per Burr"

The GI (Geographical Indication) protection system lets the national government register and protect the names of products whose qualities are tied to where they come from, such as the local climate and environment or particular production methods. Kasho Fugetsu's chestnut yokan uses a chestnut registered under this system.

What sets it apart is that there is "only one nut per burr." A chestnut burr usually holds several nuts, so the phrase means these chestnuts grow with just a single nut inside each burr. Between its nationally registered origin and this rarity, it fully earns the name "phantom chestnut."

Yokan is a traditional sweet that lets the flavor of its ingredients come through clearly. Chestnut lovers will want to see what this special chestnut becomes in a bar of yokan.

### A Kasho Fugetsu Sweet, Available in Ueno

Kasho Fugetsu is a confectioner based in Ibaraki Prefecture. This appearance is a rare chance to pick up chestnut yokan from a local Ibaraki confectioner in Tokyo, without traveling all the way to Ibaraki.

### At Matsuzakaya Ueno, Ueno's Department Store

The yokan is sold at Matsuzakaya Ueno, a department store based in Ueno. It is easy to drop by while shopping or exploring the Ueno and Okachimachi area. If you are looking for an autumn gift, or a seasonal treat for yourself, it is worth considering.

## At a Glance

- **Product**: Chestnut yokan from Kasho Fugetsu (Ibaraki)
- **Highlight**: Made with a GI-registered chestnut that has "only one nut per burr"
- **Occasion**: Released for Japanese Chestnut Day on September 30

# Nakatsugawa, Gifu Wagashi Shop "Matsuba" Opens Pop-Up at ecute Ueno

Matsuba was founded in 1950 (Showa 25). Since then, it has been making sweets in Nakatsugawa using ingredients from each of the four seasons. In the world of wagashi, where the changing seasons matter, it is a shop that has stayed committed to working with whatever each season brings.

The pop-up runs from late September to mid-October, in early autumn. It's a chance to enjoy, in Ueno at the start of autumn, sweets from a shop that values seasonal ingredients. For those who already know the shop, it's a rare chance to enjoy flavors from far away close to home. Whether you want something to go with your tea or are looking for an autumn gift, it's worth stopping by.

Matsuba was founded in 1950 (Showa 25). Products from a shop that has been making sweets in Nakatsugawa for decades are coming to Ueno.

## Taito City Launches Initiatives for a "Sustainable Tourist Destination"

As part of its effort to build a sustainable tourist destination, Taito City will run patrols with the "Taito Cleanup Cart" and carry out tourism initiatives for visitors both before their trip ("tabi-mae") and during their trip ("tabi-naka").

## Overview of the Initiatives

Taito City has many areas that draw large numbers of tourists, including Ueno. These initiatives fall under the banner of "building a sustainable tourist destination." Their aim is to welcome tourists while keeping tourism in balance with the local environment and residents' daily lives.

One pillar is the patrols of the "Taito Cleanup Cart." As the name suggests, this appears to be an effort to keep the streets clean. As tourist numbers grow, keeping the city clean becomes important for residents and visitors alike. By launching an initiative with this name, the city seems to be signaling that it wants tourism and the environment to coexist.

The other pillar is a set of tourism initiatives aimed at the "tabi-mae" and "tabi-naka" stages. "Tabi-mae" means the time before a trip, when travelers gather information about their destination and make plans. "Tabi-naka" means the trip itself, when visitors walk around town, go sightseeing, and enjoy food and drink. By offering measures for each stage, the city appears to be aiming to connect tourists with the local community throughout their journey, from before they arrive to their time on the ground.

What sets these initiatives apart is that street cleaning by the "Taito Cleanup Cart" and the pre-trip and on-trip tourism measures are pursued together under one theme: "building a sustainable tourist destination." The goal is a city where tourists can have a more comfortable stay, and where residents can benefit from tourism while keeping the neighborhood a good place to live. The initiatives reflect Taito City's commitment to achieving both.

Details such as the patrol routes, schedule, and the specific pre-trip and on-trip measures are expected in future announcements from Taito City. Whether you're visiting Ueno or live here, keep an eye out for changes around town.

For three days, from Friday, October 23 to Sunday, October 25, 2026, the Japanese Food Culture Heritage Society will hold an "Imoni-kai" (taro stew gathering) at the Benten-mon Gate Plaza in Ueno Onshi Park. This is the second edition of the event.

As its name suggests, the organizer, the Japanese Food Culture Heritage Society, is dedicated to preserving Japan's food culture and passing it on to the next generation. Following last year's event, this second edition will show whether the gathering becomes an established autumn fixture in Ueno.

"Imoni" is a hot-pot dish starring taro, an autumn favorite enjoyed especially in the Tohoku region. Seasonings and ingredients vary by region and household, making it a dish known for strongly reflecting local food culture. Gathering outdoors around a large pot during the harvest season, known as an "imoni-kai," has also long been a beloved autumn tradition in these areas. It is interesting that a society devoted to passing on Japanese food culture has chosen imoni as its theme.

The venue, the Benten-mon Gate Plaza, is located in the part of Ueno Onshi Park near Shinobazu Pond.
